statements.subject: server
statements.description: A host should not act as a DHCP server unless explicitly configured to do so by a system administrator.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: After obtaining parameters via DHCP, a DHCP client should be able to exchange packets with any other host in the Internet.

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: A client and server may negotiate for the transmission of only those parameters required by the client or specific to a particular subnet.

statements.subject: dhcp
statements.description: DHCP should be a mechanism rather than a policy.

statements.subject: dhcp
statements.description: DHCP must allow local system administrators control over configuration parameters where desired

statements.subject: user
statements.description: local system administrators should be able to enforce local policies concerning allocation and access to local resources where desired.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Clients should require no manual configuration.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Each client should be able to discover appropriate local configuration parameters without user intervention and incorporate those parameters into its own configuration.

statements.subject: dhcp
statements.description: Networks should require no manual configuration for individual clients.

statements.subject: user
statements.description: Under normal circumstances, the network manager should not have to enter any per-client configuration parameters.

statements.subject: dhcp
statements.description: DHCP should not require a server on each subnet.

statements.subject: dhcp
statements.description: DHCP must work across routers or through the intervention of BOOTP relay agents.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A DHCP client must be prepared to receive multiple responses to a request for configuration parameters.
actions: Accept and process multiple DHCP response messages received in reply to a single configuration request

statements.subject: dhcp
statements.description: DHCP must coexist with statically configured, non-participating hosts and with existing network protocol implementations.

statements.subject: dhcp
statements.description: DHCP must interoperate with the BOOTP relay agent behavior as described by RFC 951 and by RFC 1542 [21].

statements.subject: server
statements.description: DHCP must provide service to existing BOOTP clients.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: DHCP must: Guarantee that any specific network address will not be in use by more than one DHCP client at a time,
actions: Verify that the candidate address is not currently bound to any other active DHCP client before completing allocation

statements.subject: server
statements.description: DHCP must: Retain DHCP client configuration across DHCP client reboot.
actions: Persist client configuration binding to stable storage so the binding survives client reboot

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A DHCP client should, whenever possible, be assigned the same configuration parameters (e.g., network address) in response to each request,
actions: Assign the same configuration parameters to a returning client that previously held an assignment, whenever possible

statements.subject: server
statements.description: DHCP must: Retain DHCP client configuration across server reboots,
actions: Persist all active client configuration bindings to stable storage so they survive server restart

statements.subject: server
statements.description: whenever possible, a DHCP client should be assigned the same configuration parameters despite restarts of the DHCP mechanism,
actions: Assign the same configuration parameters to a client despite restarts of the DHCP mechanism whenever possible

statements.subject: dhcp
statements.description: DHCP must: Allow automated assignment of configuration parameters to new clients to avoid hand configuration for new clients,

statements.subject: dhcp
statements.description: DHCP must: Support fixed or permanent allocation of configuration parameters to specific clients.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The 'client identifier' chosen by a DHCP client MUST be unique to that client within the subnet to which the client is attached.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client uses a 'client identifier' in one message, it MUST use that same identifier in all subsequent messages, to ensure that all servers correctly identify the client.
actions: include same client identifier in all subsequent messages

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The TCP/IP software SHOULD accept and forward to the IP layer any IP packets delivered to the client's hardware address before the IP address is configured; DHCP servers and BOOTP relay agents may not be able to deliver DHCP messages to clients that cannot accept hardware unicast datagrams before the TCP/IP software is configured.
actions: accept IP packets delivered to client hardware address
forward received IP packets to IP layer

statements.subject: message
statements.description: They MUST be set to zero by clients and ignored by servers and relay agents.
actions: set reserved flags field bits to zero (client)
ignore reserved flags field bits (server)
ignore reserved flags field bits (relay agent)

statements.subject: dhcp
statements.description: For example, the key might be the pair (IP-subnet-number, hardware-address) (note that the "hardware-address" should be typed by the type of hardware to accommodate possible duplication of hardware addresses resulting from bit-ordering problems in a mixed-media, bridged network) allowing for serial or concurrent reuse of a hardware address on different subnets, and for hardware addresses that may not be globally unique.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client may extend its lease with subsequent requests.
actions: send lease extension request to server

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client may issue a message to release the address back to the server when the client no longer needs the address.
actions: send DHCPRELEASE to server

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client may ask for a permanent assignment by asking for an infinite lease.
actions: set requested lease duration to infinite in address request message

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Even when assigning "permanent" addresses, a server may choose to give out lengthy but non-infinite leases to allow detection of the fact that the client has been retired.
actions: assign lengthy non-infinite lease duration instead of infinite

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server should use whatever information is available in the configuration information repository to choose an address to reuse.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: For example, the server may choose the least recently assigned address.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: As a consistency check, the allocating server SHOULD probe the reused address before allocating the address, e.g., with an ICMP echo request, and the client SHOULD probe the newly received address, e.g., with ARP.
actions: probe reused address with ICMP echo request before completing allocation

statements.subject: message
statements.description: One particular option - the "DHCP message type" option - must be included in every DHCP message.
actions: include 'DHCP message type' option in every DHCP message sent

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Additional options may be allowed, required, or not allowed, depending on the DHCP message type.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The DHCPDISCOVER message MAY include options that suggest values for the network address and lease duration.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When allocating a new address, servers SHOULD check that the offered network address is not already in use; e.g., the server may probe the offered address with an ICMP Echo Request.
actions: check_offered_address_not_already_in_use

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers SHOULD be implemented so that network administrators MAY choose to disable probes of newly allocated addresses.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client broadcasts a DHCPREQUEST message that MUST include the 'server identifier' option to indicate which server it has selected, and that MAY include other options specifying desired configuration values.
actions: include_server_identifier_option_in_DHCPREQUEST

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The 'requested IP address' option MUST be set to the value of 'yiaddr' in the DHCPOFFER message from the server.
actions: set_requested_IP_address_option_to_DHCPOFFER_yiaddr

statements.subject: message
statements.description: To help ensure that any BOOTP relay agents forward the DHCPREQUEST message to the same set of DHCP servers that received the original DHCPDISCOVER message, the DHCPREQUEST message MUST use the same value in the DHCP message header's 'secs' field and be sent to the same IP broadcast address as the original DHCPDISCOVER message.
actions: use_same_secs_value_as_DHCPDISCOVER
send_to_same_broadcast_address_as_DHCPDISCOVER

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Any configuration parameters in the DHCPACK message SHOULD NOT conflict with those in the earlier DHCPOFFER message to which the client is responding.
actions: ensure_DHCPACK_configuration_params_do_not_conflict_with_DHCPOFFER

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server SHOULD NOT check the offered network address at this point.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the selected server is unable to satisfy the DHCPREQUEST message (e.g., the requested network address has been allocated), the server SHOULD respond with a DHCPNAK message.
actions: send_DHCPNAK

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server MAY choose to mark addresses offered to clients in DHCPOFFER messages as unavailable.
actions: mark_offered_address_as_unavailable

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server SHOULD mark an address offered to a client in a DHCPOFFER message as available if the server receives no DHCPREQUEST message from that client.
actions: mark_offered_address_as_available

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client SHOULD perform a final check on the parameters (e.g., ARP for allocated network address), and notes the duration of the lease specified in the DHCPACK message.
actions: perform_final_parameter_check
note_lease_duration_from_DHCPACK

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client detects that the address is already in use (e.g., through the use of ARP), the client MUST send a DHCPDECLINE message to the server and restarts the configuration process.
actions: send_DHCPDECLINE
restart_configuration_process

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: The client SHOULD wait a minimum of ten seconds before restarting the configuration process to avoid excessive network traffic in case of looping.
actions: wait_minimum_10_seconds_before_restarting_configuration_process

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client SHOULD notify the user that the initialization process has failed and is restarting.
statements.pre_cond: client.DHCPACK_received = false & client.DHCPNAK_received = false & client.retransmission_algorithm_complete = true
actions: notify_user_initialization_failed_and_restarting

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client used a 'client identifier' when it obtained the lease, it MUST use the same 'client identifier' in the DHCPRELEASE message.
actions: use_same_client_identifier_in_DHCPRELEASE

statements.subject: client
statements.description: As the client has not received its network address, it MUST NOT fill in the 'ciaddr' field.
actions: Do not fill in the 'ciaddr' field in DHCPREQUEST

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client used a 'client identifier' to obtain its address, the client MUST use the same 'client identifier' in the DHCPREQUEST message.
actions: Include the same 'client identifier' in the DHCPREQUEST message

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers SHOULD NOT check that the client's network address is already in use; the client may respond to ICMP Echo Request messages at this point.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the client's request is invalid (e.g., the client has moved to a new subnet), servers SHOULD respond with a DHCPNAK message to the client.
actions: send DHCPNAK to client

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers SHOULD NOT respond if their information is not guaranteed to be accurate.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: For example, a server that identifies a request for an expired binding that is owned by another server SHOULD NOT respond with a DHCPNAK unless the servers are using an explicit mechanism to maintain coherency among the servers.
statements.pre_cond: server.binding_expired = true & server.binding_owner != server.self & server.explicit_coherency_mechanism = false

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST broadcast the DHCPNAK message to the 0xffffffff broadcast address because the client may not have a correct network address or subnet mask, and the client may not be answering ARP requests.
actions: broadcast DHCPNAK to 0xffffffff broadcast address

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Otherwise, the server MUST send the DHCPNAK message to the IP address of the BOOTP relay agent, as recorded in 'giaddr'.
actions: send DHCPNAK to IP address of BOOTP relay agent recorded in giaddr

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client detects that the IP address in the DHCPACK message is already in use, the client MUST send a DHCPDECLINE message to the server and restarts the configuration process by requesting a new network address.
actions: send DHCPDECLINE to server
restart configuration process by requesting a new network address

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client receives neither a DHCPACK or a DHCPNAK message after employing the retransmission algorithm, the client MAY choose to use the previously allocated network address and configuration parameters for the remainder of the unexpired lease.
statements.pre_cond: client.received_DHCPACK = false & client.received_DHCPNAK = false & client.retransmission_algorithm_complete = true & client.lease_unexpired = true
actions: use previously allocated network address and configuration parameters for remainder of unexpired lease

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client acquires a lease for a network address for a fixed period of time (which may be infinite).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If there is drift between the two clocks, the server may consider the lease expired before the client does.
actions: server marks lease as expired in its local database

statements.subject: server
statements.description: To compensate, the server may return a shorter lease duration to the client than the server commits to its local database of client information.
actions: server includes shorter lease duration value in outbound DHCP message to client
server stores longer lease duration in local client database

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If a client has obtained a network address through some other means (e.g., manual configuration), it may use a DHCPINFORM request message to obtain other local configuration parameters.
actions: send DHCPINFORM request message

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The servers SHOULD unicast the DHCPACK reply to the address given in the 'ciaddr' field of the DHCPINFORM message.
actions: unicast DHCPACK reply to ciaddr field of DHCPINFORM

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server SHOULD check the network address in a DHCPINFORM message for consistency, but MUST NOT check for an existing lease.
actions: check network address in DHCPINFORM for consistency

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Second, in its initial DHCPDISCOVER or DHCPREQUEST message, a client may provide the server with a list of specific parameters the client is interested in.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client includes a list of parameters in a DHCPDISCOVER message, it MUST include that list in any subsequent DHCPREQUEST messages.
actions: include in DHCPREQUEST the same parameter list sent in DHCPDISCOVER

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client SHOULD include the 'maximum DHCP message size' option to let the server know how large the server may make its DHCP messages.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client may include the 'requested IP address' option to suggest that a particular IP address be assigned, and may include the 'IP address lease time' option to suggest the lease time it would like.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: However, additional options may be ignored by servers, and multiple servers may, therefore, not return identical values for some options.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If a server receives a DHCPREQUEST message with an invalid 'requested IP address', the server SHOULD respond to the client with a DHCPNAK message and may choose to report the problem to the system administrator.
actions: send DHCPNAK to client

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server may include an error message in the 'message' option.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client with multiple network interfaces must use DHCP through each interface independently to obtain configuration information parameters for those separate interfaces.
statements.post_cond: forall i in client.interfaces: session.dhcp_initiated(i) = true
actions: initiate_independent_DHCP_session_per_interface

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client SHOULD use DHCP to reacquire or verify its IP address and network parameters whenever the local network parameters may have changed; e.g., at system boot time or after a disconnection from the local network, as the local network configuration may change without the client's or user's knowledge.
actions: use DHCP to reacquire or verify IP address and network parameters

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If a client has knowledge of a previous network address and is unable to contact a local DHCP server, the client may continue to use the previous network address until the lease for that address expires.
actions: continue to use previous network address until lease expires

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the lease expires before the client can contact a DHCP server, the client must immediately discontinue use of the previous network address and may inform local users of the problem.
actions: immediately discontinue use of previous network address

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server with multiple network address (e.g., a multi-homed host) MAY use any of its network addresses in outgoing DHCP messages.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server with multiple network addresses MUST be prepared to to accept any of its network addresses as identifying that server in a DHCP message.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: To accommodate potentially incomplete network connectivity, a server MUST choose an address as a 'server identifier' that, to the best of the server's knowledge, is reachable from the client.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: For example, if the DHCP server and the DHCP client are connected to the same subnet (i.e., the 'giaddr' field in the message from the client is zero), the server SHOULD select the IP address the server is using for communication on that subnet as the 'server identifier'.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server has received a message through a DHCP relay agent, the server SHOULD choose an address from the interface on which the message was recieved as the 'server identifier' (unless the server has other, better information on which to make its choice).

statements.subject: client
statements.description: DHCP clients MUST use the IP address provided in the 'server identifier' option for any unicast requests to the DHCP server.
actions: use IP address from 'server identifier' option as unicast destination for all DHCP requests to server

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If the options in a DHCP message extend into the 'sname' and 'file' fields, the 'option overload' option MUST appear in the 'options' field, with value 1, 2 or 3, as specified in RFC 1533.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If the 'option overload' option is present in the 'options' field, the options in the 'options' field MUST be terminated by an 'end' option, and MAY contain one or more 'pad' options to fill the options field.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The options in the 'sname' and 'file' fields (if in use as indicated by the 'options overload' option) MUST begin with the first octet of the field, MUST be terminated by an 'end' option, and MUST be followed by 'pad' options to fill the remainder of the field.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Any individual option in the 'options', 'sname' and 'file' fields MUST be entirely contained in that field.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The options in the 'options' field MUST be interpreted first, so that any 'option overload' options may be interpreted.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The 'file' field MUST be interpreted next (if the 'option overload' option indicates that the 'file' field contains DHCP options), followed by the 'sname' field.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MUST adopt a retransmission strategy that incorporates a randomized exponential backoff algorithm to determine the delay between retransmissions.
actions: apply randomized exponential backoff algorithm to compute delay before each retransmission

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: The delay between retransmissions SHOULD be chosen to allow sufficient time for replies from the server to be delivered based on the characteristics of the internetwork between the client and the server.
actions: choose retransmission delay sufficient to allow server reply delivery given internetwork characteristics

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: For example, in a 10Mb/sec Ethernet internetwork, the delay before the first retransmission SHOULD be 4 seconds randomized by the value of a uniform random number chosen from the range -1 to +1.
actions: set first retransmission delay to 4 seconds randomized by uniform random value in [-1, +1]

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: The delay before the next retransmission SHOULD be 8 seconds randomized by the value of a uniform number chosen from the range -1 to +1.
actions: set second retransmission delay to 8 seconds randomized by uniform random value in [-1, +1]

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: The retransmission delay SHOULD be doubled with subsequent retransmissions up to a maximum of 64 seconds.
actions: double retransmission delay on each subsequent retransmission
cap retransmission delay at 64 seconds

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MAY provide an indication of retransmission attempts to the user as an indication of the progress of the configuration process.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A DHCP client MUST choose 'xid's in such a way as to minimize the chance of using an 'xid' identical to one used by another client.
actions: select xid to minimize probability of collision with xids used by other clients

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client that cannot receive unicast IP datagrams until its protocol software has been configured with an IP address SHOULD set the BROADCAST bit in the 'flags' field to 1 in any DHCPDISCOVER or DHCPREQUEST messages that client sends.
actions: set BROADCAST bit in 'flags' field to 1 in DHCPDISCOVER and DHCPREQUEST messages

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client that can receive unicast IP datagrams before its protocol software has been configured SHOULD clear the BROADCAST bit to 0.
actions: clear BROADCAST bit in 'flags' field to 0

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server or relay agent sending or relaying a DHCP message directly to a DHCP client (i.e., not to a relay agent specified in the 'giaddr' field) SHOULD examine the BROADCAST bit in the 'flags' field.
actions: examine BROADCAST bit in 'flags' field before sending or relaying message directly to client

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If this bit is set to 1, the DHCP message SHOULD be sent as an IP broadcast using an IP broadcast address (preferably 0xffffffff) as the IP destination address and the link-layer broadcast address as the link-layer destination address.
actions: send DHCP message as IP broadcast using 0xffffffff as IP destination and link-layer broadcast as link-layer destination

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If the BROADCAST bit is cleared to 0, the message SHOULD be sent as an IP unicast to the IP address specified in the 'yiaddr' field and the link-layer address specified in the 'chaddr' field.
actions: send DHCP message as IP unicast to 'yiaddr' with link-layer destination set to 'chaddr'

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If unicasting is not possible, the message MAY be sent as an IP broadcast using an IP broadcast address (preferably 0xffffffff) as the IP destination address and the link-layer broadcast address as the link-layer destination address.
actions: send DHCP message as IP broadcast to 0xffffffff with link-layer broadcast destination when unicasting is not possible

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MAY choose to explicitly provide the identifier through the 'client identifier' option.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client supplies a 'client identifier', the client MUST use the same 'client identifier' in all subsequent messages, and the server MUST use that identifier to identify the client.
actions: include same 'client identifier' option value in all subsequent protocol messages

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the client does not provide a 'client identifier' option, the server MUST use the contents of the 'chaddr' field to identify the client.
actions: use contents of 'chaddr' field as the key to identify and associate client with its lease

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client implementation of DHCP SHOULD provide a mechanism for the user to select directly the 'vendor class identifier' values.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If an address is available, the new address SHOULD be chosen as follows:
actions: select_new_address_per_priority_rules

statements.subject: server
statements.description: As described in section 4.2, a server MAY, for administrative reasons, assign an address other than the one requested, or may refuse to allocate an address to a particular client even though free addresses are available.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: While not required for correct operation of DHCP, the server SHOULD NOT reuse the selected network address before the client responds to the server's DHCPOFFER message.
actions: retain_offered_address_as_unavailable_until_client_responds

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The configuration parameters MUST be selected by applying the following rules in the order given below.
actions: apply_parameter_selection_rules_in_specified_order

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST return to the client:
actions: send_DHCPOFFER_with_network_address_lease_expiration_and_requested_parameters

statements.subject: server
statements.description: IF the server has been explicitly configured with a default value for the parameter, the server MUST include that value in an appropriate option in the 'option' field, ELSE

statements.subject: server
statements.description: IF the server recognizes the parameter as a parameter defined in the Host Requirements Document, the server MUST include the default value for that parameter as given in the Host Requirements Document in an appropriate option in the 'option' field, ELSE

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST NOT return a value for that parameter,

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST supply as many of the requested parameters as possible and MUST omit any parameters it cannot provide.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST include each requested parameter only once unless explicitly allowed in the DHCP Options and BOOTP Vendor Extensions document.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: the parameters MUST be identified by an exact match between the client's vendor class identifiers and the client's classes identified in the server,

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MAY choose to return the 'vendor class identifier' used to determine the parameters in the DHCPOFFER message to assist the client in selecting which DHCPOFFER to accept.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client uses a 'client identifier' in a DHCPREQUEST message, it MUST use that same 'client identifier' in all subsequent messages.
actions: use same 'client identifier' in all subsequent messages

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client included a list of requested parameters in a DHCPDISCOVER message, it MUST include that list in all subsequent messages.
actions: include requested parameter list in all subsequent messages

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client SHOULD use the parameters in the DHCPACK message for configuration.
actions: use DHCPACK parameters for configuration

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Client inserts the address of the selected server in 'server identifier', 'ciaddr' MUST be zero, 'requested IP address' MUST be filled in with the yiaddr value from the chosen DHCPOFFER.
actions: insert selected server address in 'server identifier'
set ciaddr to zero
fill 'requested IP address' with yiaddr from chosen DHCPOFFER

statements.subject: server
statements.description: As an implementation detail, servers SHOULD NOT reuse offered addresses and may use an implementation-specific timeout mechanism to decide when to reuse an offered address.
actions: do not reuse offered addresses

statements.subject: client
statements.description: 'server identifier' MUST NOT be filled in, 'requested IP address' option MUST be filled in with client's notion of its previously assigned address.
actions: do not fill 'server identifier'

statements.subject: client
statements.description: 'ciaddr' MUST be zero.
actions: set ciaddr to zero

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Server SHOULD send a DHCPNAK message to the client if the 'requested IP address' is incorrect, or is on the wrong network.
actions: send DHCPNAK to client

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the DHCP server detects that the client is on the wrong net (i.e., the result of applying the local subnet mask or remote subnet mask (if 'giaddr' is not zero) to 'requested IP address' option value doesn't match reality), then the server SHOULD send a DHCPNAK message to the client.

actions: send DHCPNAK to client

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If not, then the server SHOULD send a DHCPNAK message to the client.
actions: send DHCPNAK to client

statements.description: If the DHCP server has no record of this client, then it MUST remain silent, and MAY output a warning to the network administrator.

actions: remain silent (do not respond to DHCPREQUEST)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST set the broadcast bit in the DHCPNAK, so that the relay agent will broadcast the DHCPNAK to the client, because the client may not have a correct network address or subnet mask, and the client may not be answering ARP requests.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: |requested-ip  |MUST         | (Table 4, INIT-REBOOT column: requested-ip MUST)
actions: Include requested-ip option in outgoing client message

statements.subject: client
statements.description: |requested-ip  |MUST         | (Table 4, SELECTING column: requested-ip MUST)
actions: Include requested-ip option in outgoing client message

statements.subject: client
statements.description: |requested-ip  |MUST NOT     | (Table 4, RENEWING column: requested-ip MUST NOT)
actions: Omit requested-ip option from outgoing client message

statements.subject: client
statements.description: |requested-ip  |MUST NOT  | (Table 4, REBINDING column: requested-ip MUST NOT)
actions: Omit requested-ip option from outgoing client message

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client SHOULD wait a random time between one and ten seconds to desynchronize the use of DHCP at startup.
actions: wait random time between 1 and 10 seconds before broadcasting DHCPDISCOVER

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MAY request specific parameters by including the 'parameter request list' option.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MAY suggest a network address and/or lease time by including the 'requested IP address' and 'IP address lease time' options.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MUST include its hardware address in the 'chaddr' field, if necessary for delivery of DHCP reply messages.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MAY include a different unique identifier in the 'client identifier' option, as discussed in section 4.2.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the 'xid' of an arriving DHCPOFFER message does not match the 'xid' of the most recent DHCPDISCOVER message, the DHCPOFFER message must be silently discarded.
actions: silently discard DHCPOFFER message

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Any arriving DHCPACK messages must be silently discarded.
actions: silently discard DHCPACK message

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client SHOULD perform a check on the suggested address to ensure that the address is not already in use.
actions: perform address-in-use check on suggested address (e.g., ARP probe)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When broadcasting an ARP request for the suggested address, the client must fill in its own hardware address as the sender's hardware address, and 0 as the sender's IP address, to avoid confusing ARP caches in other hosts on the same subnet.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the network address appears to be in use, the client MUST send a DHCPDECLINE message to the server.
actions: send DHCPDECLINE message to server

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client SHOULD broadcast an ARP reply to announce the client's new IP address and clear any outdated ARP cache entries in hosts on the client's subnet.
actions: broadcast ARP reply to announce new IP address and clear outdated ARP cache entries on subnet

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MUST insert its known network address as a 'requested IP address' option in the DHCPREQUEST message.
actions: Insert client known network address as 'requested IP address' option in DHCPREQUEST message

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client may request specific configuration parameters by including the 'parameter request list' option.
actions: Optionally include 'parameter request list' option in DHCPREQUEST message

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MUST NOT include a 'server identifier' in the DHCPREQUEST message.
actions: Omit 'server identifier' option from DHCPREQUEST message

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client SHOULD NOT request lease time parameters.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: DHCPINFORM messages MUST be directed to the 'DHCP server' UDP port.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client does not receive a DHCPACK within a reasonable period of time (60 seconds or 4 tries if using timeout suggested in section 4.1), then it SHOULD display a message informing the user of the problem, and then SHOULD begin network processing using suitable defaults as per Appendix A.
actions: display message to user informing of the problem
begin network processing using suitable defaults per Appendix A

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When the DHCP client knows the address of a DHCP server, in either INIT or REBOOTING state, the client may use that address in the DHCPDISCOVER or DHCPREQUEST rather than the IP broadcast address.
actions: use known server unicast address as destination instead of IP broadcast address in DHCPDISCOVER or DHCPREQUEST

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client may also use unicast to send DHCPINFORM messages to a known DHCP server.
actions: send DHCPINFORM via unicast to known DHCP server address

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: T1 MUST be earlier than T2, which, in turn, MUST be earlier than the time at which the client's lease will expire.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: Times T1 and T2 SHOULD be chosen with some random "fuzz" around a fixed value, to avoid synchronization of client reacquisition.
actions: apply random fuzz to T1 and T2 values around their fixed base values to prevent synchronized client reacquisition

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MAY choose to extend the client's lease according to policy set by the network administrator.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server SHOULD return T1 and T2, and their values SHOULD be adjusted from their original values to take account of the time remaining on the lease.
actions: include T1 option in DHCPACK adjusted for time remaining on lease
include T2 option in DHCPACK adjusted for time remaining on lease

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In both RENEWING and REBINDING states, if the client receives no response to its DHCPREQUEST message, the client SHOULD wait one-half of the remaining time until T2 (in RENEWING state) and one-half of the remaining lease time (in REBINDING state), down to a minimum of 60 seconds, before retransmitting the DHCPREQUEST message.
actions: if client.state = RENEWING: wait max(60s, 0.5 * (T2 - current_time)) before retransmitting DHCPREQUEST
if client.state = REBINDING: wait max(60s, 0.5 * remaining_lease_time) before retransmitting DHCPREQUEST

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the lease expires before the client receives a DHCPACK, the client moves to INIT state, MUST immediately stop any other network processing and requests network initialization parameters as if the client were uninitialized.
actions: move to INIT state
immediately stop all other network processing
request network initialization parameters as if uninitialized

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client then receives a DHCPACK allocating that client its previous network address, the client SHOULD continue network processing.
actions: resume network processing with previously held network address

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client is given a new network address, it MUST NOT continue using the previous network address and SHOULD notify the local users of the problem.
actions: cease using previous network address immediately
